races.name: Big Stage Hire Amateur Jockeys' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Sea Of Charm
runners_data.note: An 8-year-old who has run consistently at 12f but steps up to 1m6f today; her best form at this distance is unproven, and despite a trainer in poor recent form (0 wins from 3 in 14 days), she is shown on the lead as the default pace-setter — though her natural inclination is to race off the pace, which will likely produce a slow gallop rather than a true searching test|
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in her last six starts, Sea Of Charm nonetheless brings strong fitness on 16 days' rest, experience over today's trip and going, and a third last time out that gives her a narrow edge in this small field — our rating of 68 makes her the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Belle Of Kt
runners_data.note: Arrives in excellent recent form with a win included in her last six, and trainer J S Moore has been active and placing horses well (2/11 in 14 days); genuinely a hold-up operator who will want cover before making her challenge, and although this firm ground is a slight unknown compared to her Standard surface wins, her age and consistency at 10-12f makes the step to 1m6f a manageable ask|
runners_data.comment: Belle Of Kt won last time out and has run over today's trip, arriving here just eight days later in fine form — the main question is whether 151 lb tests her stamina under that weight.

runners_data.name: Bumaan
runners_data.note: A lightly-raced three-year-old whose form shows repeated placed efforts at staying trips, including two seconds at 10-12f, suggesting genuine stamina; George Boughey's yard is in fair form (3/23 in 14 days) and this horse carries headgear (t), which combined with the step to the longest trip he has attempted, makes him an interesting unknown — he is a hold-up horse who may need to be more patient than ideal in a small, slow-run field|
runners_data.comment: Bumaan has finished second in each of his last two starts, and with just 15 days between runs he arrives in peak freshness — the main risk is that he remains winless in recent starts despite those near-misses.

runners_data.name: Fabled Spirit
runners_data.note: The concern with Fabled Spirit is explicit — she fades in the finish — and a slowly-run race over 1m6f on Firm ground that ends in a sprint is almost the worst possible scenario for her profile; 46 days off the track, a form string of 0-8-0 in three runs, and a jockey with limited mounts make this a horse to treat with significant caution, even though Archie Watson is capable of placing horses well|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts and ranked fourth on our rating, Fabled Spirit's chief appeal lies in his 46-day freshness and the weight he carries at 142 lb — though his recent string of unplaced efforts is the obvious concern.

races.paceDynamic: Sea Of Charm is the only horse with any front-running credentials in this four-runner field, and although her true style is hold-up, she is the most likely pace-setter by default on a Firm Bath track over 1m6f with no natural leader to challenge her. With Sea Of Charm redistributed to the front, the tempo is likely to be steady and controlled rather than searching, which on firm ground over this marathon trip will compress the field and invite a late sprint finish. The remaining three runners — Belle Of Kt, Bumaan, and Fabled Spirit — are all genuine hold-up or wait-and-pounce types who will race in a tight bunch behind, meaning the race will be decided in the final two furlongs with little separation until then. This shape strongly favours the runner with the best finishing kick and ability to quicken on firm ground from a mid-to-rear position, particularly one with proven form at this sort of trip. This field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Belle Of Kt and Fabled Spirit are true back-of-the-field operators, but with only four runners, the bunch will be compact enough that the distinction between midfield and rear matters less than raw finishing ability.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Late Sprint
scenarios.trigger: If Sea Of Charm sets a modest, uncontested gallop and the field coasts into the straight before quickening
scenarios.body: Sea Of Charm dictates a dawdling tempo on firm ground, and the race ignites only in the final two furlongs as the hold-up horses launch their challenges in a sprint finish; on firm Bath turf this suits the horse with the sharpest acceleration and best recent form at the trip

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Bumaan Steps Forward
scenarios.trigger: If Bumaan tracks close to the pace throughout and outstays the others with his improving profile at the longer trip
scenarios.body: Still only three years old and stepping up from 10f to 1m6f, Bumaan has shown consistent placed form at stays distances and on a firm surface the extra ground could unlock his stamina; his trainer George Boughey has a solid 14-day record and a prominent tracking run could see him wear down tiring rivals

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Belle Of Kt Confirms Class
scenarios.trigger: If Belle Of Kt's recent winning form on Standard surfaces translates to Firm ground and she delivers her challenge at the right moment
scenarios.body: Belle Of Kt brings the best recent form in the field with a win last time, and her consistent placed efforts over 10-12f suggest the 1m6f trip is within range; the reduced competitive edge of an amateur jockeys' race could allow her to coast into contention and produce her usual late effort without facing overly aggressive tactics

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Fabled Spirit Galvanises
scenarios.trigger: If Fabled Spirit's 46-day break has freshened her and she overcomes her noted tendency to fade in the finish
scenarios.body: Fabled Spirit has struggled on Good ground in her three runs and the switch to Firm could theoretically help, but her finishing record shows a consistent fade which works directly against a slow-run race that will end in a sprint; the layoff and Archie Watson's one winner from fourteen in 14 days means this scenario depends on too many unknowns aligning

watchPoints.text: Watch Sea Of Charm's early behaviour — if she drifts back to her natural position and no horse picks up the lead, the field could effectively walk the first mile with chaotic late consequences for all runners|

Belle Of Kt's going experience is primarily on Standard surfaces; on Firm Bath turf today, watch how she moves through the early stages — any sign of discomfort could explain a below-par finish despite her strong recent form|
Bumaan's stamina for 1m6f is genuinely untested — all his best form has come at 10-12f — so watch whether he begins to weaken after the two-furlong pole as the extra ground potentially found him out|

With only four runners and a probable slow early tempo, jockey positioning in the back straight will be critical; watch whether Miss Scarlett Dorricott (Belle Of Kt, 5lb claim) and Mr Henry Callan (Bumaan) move up to track Sea Of Charm early or elect to fill the entire straight with a late run|

Fabled Spirit's 46-day absence is notable — watch her in the paddock and early in the race for signs of freshness or ring-rustiness, as either extreme will influence whether she can overcome her pattern of fading late|

runners_data.name: Sheer Beauty
runners_data.note: Won on firm over 5f last time out, giving her direct course-and-going form that few rivals can match; sits naturally prominent which is the ideal tactical slot in this pace setup, and Dylan Hogan's low-key booking masks a horse whose profile fits this race shape very well.

runners_data.name: Crimson Blaze
runners_data.note: Richard Hughes has been in decent recent form (4/27 over 14 days) and this filly returns after a 75-day break, but her natural hold-up style means she is unlikely to get the position she needs — she ends up racing in midfield rather than at the rear where she is most effective, compromising her genuine chance significantly.

runners_data.name: Havana Gift
runners_data.note: The most experienced hold-up performer in the field with five runs, multiple placings over 5f on good ground and a competitive 10-day turnaround; the concern is that firm Bath ground and a front-runner given a soft lead may simply leave too much to do, even for the most battle-hardened closer here.

runners_data.name: Texas Crown
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner whose OR of 120 dwarfs the handicap-banded rivals and who has placed on firm ground over 6f previously; Luke Catton (3) gets a clear lead with zero pressure expected, and the firm surface will help him maintain his gallop without being worn down — this is his race to lose.

runners_data.name: Thai Boxer
runners_data.note: Complete unknown with no public form, flagged UNKNOWN for style and going preference; Darragh Keenan takes the ride for Adrian Wintle (2/16 T14) and while debut winners do emerge at Bath, the absence of any form guide makes it impossible to assess how this runner slots into the pace scenario.

runners_data.name: Zonneveld
runners_data.note: Finished eighth on debut over 6f on good ground and is flagged as a horse that fades in the finish, which is a damaging flag in a race where the front-runner is expected to dictate; dropping to 5½f on faster ground is unlikely to reverse that tendency, and Taylor Fisher faces a stiff task from a hold-up position.

runners_data.name: Tricky Jenny
runners_data.note: Has placed on firm ground over 5f (2/5f/FIR) giving her a relevant going angle, and James Owen is the standout trainer strike rate here (16/47 over 14 days); however, her true hold-up style means she is mapped to midfield rather than her preferred rear position, and with Mason Paetel (5) claiming, the tactical disadvantage is real even if the form and trainer form are encouraging.

races.paceDynamic: Texas Crown is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with no obvious rival willing to press hard from the gates, is set to control this 5½f contest at Bath on firm ground at a sustainable, metronomic tempo. Sheer Beauty will look to sit prominently just off the leader, giving the front two a clear advantage in dictating how much energy is expended in the first two furlongs. The hold-up contingent — Havana Gift, Zonneveld, Crimson Blaze and Tricky Jenny — will be chasing from the rear across a track and going combination that historically rewards those who travel close to the pace rather than those making up ground late. This race shape strongly favours the lead-to-prominent profile: firm ground at Bath compresses the winning margin, leaves little room for closers to find their stride, and hands the initiative entirely to Texas Crown and Sheer Beauty. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can absorb at the rear — Crimson Blaze and Tricky Jenny are genuine hold-up horses redistributed to midfield because they are unlikely to secure their natural position, meaning neither is racing from an ideal base.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Texas Crown Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Texas Crown bowls along in front at a comfortable clip with no rival willing to apply early pressure.
scenarios.body: Texas Crown sets fractions to suit itself on firm Bath ground, with Sheer Beauty tracking closely in second and no closer able to generate the momentum required to peg back a front-runner given a soft lead; firm ground rewards those who have travelled efficiently throughout.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Pull Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Sheer Beauty tracks Texas Crown to within a length turning for home and outstays it in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: Sheer Beauty's form win on firm ground (1/5f/FIR) becomes directly relevant as the pace is honest enough to strip out non-stayers but not so fierce as to drain Sheer Beauty before the final furlong; the two prominent horses simply outclass the hold-up pack who cannot close the gap on fast ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Texas Crown's early tempo proves faster than it looks and the front-runners tie each other up, leaving a late gap.
scenarios.body: Havana Gift has the most consistent form of the closers, with multiple placings over this trip on good ground and a recent run just 10 days ago keeping her sharp; however, firm Bath ground and a uncontested lead make this scenario decidedly against the grain, requiring a significant pace collapse at the front.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Debutant Bolt From Blue
scenarios.trigger: If Thai Boxer, unknown in terms of style and lightly raced, shows a natural racing pattern that immediately puts it in the race.
scenarios.body: Thai Boxer's unknown style (flagged UNKNOWN) is the biggest wildcard in the field and a debut over 5½f on firm ground could reveal an undiscovered engine, but the lack of any public form, combined with a likely prominent or mid-field draw against experienced rivals, makes this a long-shot dependency on unseen ability.

watchPoints.text: Texas Crown's early sectionals are the hinge of this race — if Luke Catton (3) is able to bowl along unchallenged through the first two furlongs, the race is effectively over before the field straightens up.

Thai Boxer is a complete unknown stylistically and going-wise; if it breaks smartly and challenges Texas Crown for the lead, the tempo could lift sharply and undermine the front-runner's chance of controlling fractions.

Tricky Jenny's trainer James Owen has a hot 16/47 14-day strike rate — if Owen has this filly peaking for today, the hold-up disadvantage could be mitigated by raw ability, making her the most dangerous outsider despite her positional compromise.

Firm ground at Bath is reported consistently across all races on the card — any horse that showed going concerns on fast surfaces in its history (Crimson Blaze on soft/standard form) will find conditions less forgiving than recent runs suggest.

Havana Gift's very recent run (10 days ago) keeps her fitness sharp among the hold-up group, but her placings have all come on good ground; watch whether firm Bath terrain blunts her finishing kick in the closing 100 yards.

races.name: Bath Rum And Reggae Race Night 15th August Classified Stakes (Bath Summer Sprint Series Qualifier)

runners_data.name: Battle Point
runners_data.note: A seven-year-old who has been finishing mid-to-rear over 6f on Good at Goodwood; Gina Mangan takes over for Michael Attwater and 31 days off adds a small query, though the horse is comfortable on quick ground — pushed back on the map as the field has more closers than slots at the rear.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, with a pair of sevenths in his most recent outings, Battle Point faces a stiff task ranked last on our figures here; stall one and experience over today's trip and going offer slim consolation.

runners_data.name: I Was Thinking
runners_data.note: Adrian Wintle's five-year-old is returning from 56 days off, the longest absence in the field, and that layoff must be flagged; a natural hold-up horse who has been ridden towards the rear, the wider field means she is unlikely to find her cleanest run, and the absence adds uncertainty.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, I Was Thinking nevertheless rates top of the field on our figures, if only narrowly, and having run over today's trip before, he arrives with solid claims — a third last time out the obvious hook, with 56 days off the only query.

runners_data.name: Jackie Brown
runners_data.note: Recent placed efforts at 5f and 6f on Good confirm she handles fast ground and sharp tracks; the lone front-runner here with Finley Marsh aboard, she wears a tongue tie and drops back from 7f — the uncontested lead is her primary asset and she must use it fully.
runners_data.comment: Placed in each of her last two starts, Jackie Brown arrives here in decent nick after a 14-day break, and has run over today's trip before; however, she remains winless in her last five starts and her official mark of 48 suggests she faces a stiff task from stall seven carrying 135 lb.

runners_data.name: Rinky Tinky Tinky
runners_data.note: Wears a hood (p) for Mrs Gavrilescu-Leveque and has run consistently around 5-6f on Good, finishing fifth twice recently; headgear often encourages early prominence, which means she could push forward from her natural hold-up tendency — Taylor Fisher is a claimer to note at these lower weights.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with finishes no better than fifth in recent outings, Rinky Tinky Tinky is hard to fancy against this field — though she has run over today's trip before and 14 days since her last run suggests she arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Sisters In The Sky
runners_data.note: Grace Harris's seven-year-old has a notable recent second on Firm over 6f, the most directly relevant similar-going evidence in this field, and she also wears a hood; a natural sit-and-wait type who could press forward given the competition for position, that Firm run gives her a clear going edge.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in his last six starts, Sisters In The Sky nevertheless brings distance and going experience to the table and is freshened up on 30 days' rest; the second last time out shows ability, though the ninth two starts back is a concern at a mark of 45.

runners_data.name: Some Nightmare
runners_data.note: William Carson — the most experienced jockey in the race — rides this nine-year-old who has been consistently placed at 5-6f on Good and Firm, including a third on Firm; genuine hold-up style that has not been disrupted by redistribution, making him a reliable profiler for the late-run scenario.
runners_data.comment: Consistently knocking on the door, Some Nightmare has finished third three times in his last six starts and arrives here fitter than most at just 15 days since his last run, with experience of today's trip and conditions; the worry is he remains winless and must prove he can finally convert.

runners_data.name: Spirited Dancer
runners_data.note: Daniel and Claire Kubler's four-year-old has placed twice over 6-7f on Good and wears a hood; dropping back to 5½f for the first time in recent runs is a distance query, though the trainer has a 3/9 strike rate in 14 days and the horse is clearly in good form.
runners_data.comment: Consecutive placed efforts two and three starts back give Spirited Dancer a live each-way profile, and she has run over today's trip before; drawn in stall 2 carrying 135 lb, the eighth last time out is the risk to weigh up.

runners_data.name: Symbol Of Hope
runners_data.note: Grace Harris again, with Callum Hutchinson in the plate; placed on both Firm runs in the last four starts, showing the going suits, and wears a hood — a natural hold-up type moved back on the map who will need the clearest of passages to land a blow from the rear.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Symbol Of Hope has been largely disappointing, with an eighth and unplaced run among the recent form; third last time out and a third four starts back offer some small comfort, and he has run over today's trip and going before, but a mark of 44 makes the task plain.

runners_data.name: Rogue Rebellion
runners_data.note: The sole three-year-old, carrying 5lbs less than most rivals at 130lbs, which is a tangible physical advantage; placed on Firm over 6f and three times in the last five, Rogue Rebellion handles quick ground but has been well beaten in two of those efforts — William Carver must find cover and deliver a timed run.
runners_data.comment: Rogue Rebellion has finished third twice in his last three starts, arriving here fit on 17 days' rest with experience of today's trip and going — his rating of 53 marks him as a genuine threat. The risk is that he remains winless in recent starts and must shoulder 130 lb from stall nine.

races.paceDynamic: Jackie Brown is the lone confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner field and, with no genuine rival to pressure her early, she is expected to bowl along at a sustainable gallop on fast ground over 5½f at Bath — a track that can reward those who get into a rhythm up front. The bulk of the field — Battle Point, I Was Thinking, Sisters In The Sky, Rinky Tinky Tinky, and Symbol Of Hope — are all natural hold-up or prominent types, but with so many of that ilk they cannot all settle into their preferred position; the most likely to actually assert and secure a forward berth from among the redistributed runners are Sisters In The Sky and Rinky Tinky Tinky, both of whom carry headgear (p) that typically encourages early engagement. On firm ground over a sprint trip with a single uncontested lead, the race shape decisively favours hold-up types who can produce a sustained late run into the straight, provided Jackie Brown does not steal an insurmountable break — the profile that benefits most is a horse capable of tracking in mid-to-rear and finishing powerfully in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Jackie Brown Leads Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Jackie Brown dictates an uncontested, metronomic fractions and her rivals fail to close the gap turning in.
scenarios.body: Jackie Brown rolls along on firm ground without a single rival prepared to chase her early, building a lead that proves beyond the hold-up field to peg back; firm ground rewards horses that settle and travel sweetly, and she was placed over this course configuration recently.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closers Swamp The Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Jackie Brown sets an overly generous tempo that leaves her vulnerable and the hold-up runners produce a coordinated finish.
scenarios.body: The hold-up horses closest to their natural position — Some Nightmare, Spirited Dancer, and Rogue Rebellion — fire late runs as the leader ties up; on firm ground the closing sectionals can be sharp and any horse with a clean passage through will be dangerous.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Fight It Out
scenarios.trigger: If Sisters In The Sky or Rinky Tinky Tinky push forward to race prominently and force a contested pace alongside Jackie Brown.
scenarios.body: The race suddenly has multiple leaders competing for the same ground, raising the tempo and potentially setting it up for a stronger stayer of the group to run through them late; Sisters In The Sky has a recent second on Firm and handles this test well.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Draw And Luck Decide
scenarios.trigger: If the field bunches in the straight with limited daylight and a horse gets a fortunate split that no pace reading could predict.
scenarios.body: A compressed finish on fast ground where the result turns on a rider's split-second decision or a gap opening at the critical moment; horses with experienced jockeys and tactical flexibility are best placed to capitalise.

watchPoints.text: Jackie Brown (Finley Marsh) — if she crosses cleanly to the rail and establishes an uncontested lead inside the first furlong, the race shape locks in around her and the hold-up field will be chasing a moving target on firm ground.

Sisters In The Sky and Rinky Tinky Tinky both wear hood headgear and are the most likely of the redistributed hold-up types to push forward early — if both engage Jackie Brown for the lead, the tempo could spike and dramatically alter the race shape.

Some Nightmare (William Carson) is the best-credentialled jockey in the field on a horse that has been consistently placed at this trip on Firm; watch whether Carson gets a clear run through in the straight, as traffic could be the decisive factor for the late-closers.

Spirited Dancer has not run below 6f in recent starts — the drop to 5½f is untested in this form cycle and Ebrahim Nader's position in the race at the two-furlong pole will indicate whether the shorter trip is catching the horse out.

I Was Thinking returns from 56 days off, the longest break of any runner; Adrian Wintle has two winners from 16 in the past 14 days but fitness after nearly two months absence over a fast-ground sprint trip is a genuine watch point.

runners_data.name: It's A Mugs Game
runners_data.note: Lightly raced 3yo returning after 331 days off for Joe Tickle; a natural hold-up horse whose sole start was a 10th over 6f on soft, making the fitness angle a real concern on this firm ground — held up by nature but pushed into a midfield slot here given the volume of off-the-pace types in the field.

runners_data.name: Kodicall
runners_data.note: J S Moore's 3yo recorded a fifth over 5f on good last time out 17 days ago, giving him a directly relevant trip and going profile; a hold-up runner who, with only six rivals and no genuine pace, is likely to find himself closer to the action than usual and could capitalise on positional clarity.

runners_data.name: Elmfield
runners_data.note: George Scott's colt has consecutive fifths and sevenths over 6f, so dropping to 5½f on faster ground is an interesting switch; by nature he settles at the back, but with the field so packed with hold-up types the map places him forward of his instinct — that redistribution tempers confidence in a strong late run.

runners_data.name: Honky Tonk Girl
runners_data.note: Oliver Cole's filly has shown a pattern of moderate finishes (5-9-4-3) and is ridden by 5lb claimer Mason Paetel; she is naturally inclined to come from off the pace, but the overcrowded hold-up sector means she is likely to find herself racing in a midfield pack rather than in isolation at the rear, and the 5½f trip looks sharp.

runners_data.name: Nzuri
runners_data.note: Gina Mangan takes the ride on this 6-run maiden whose best effort was a second over 6f on standard; headgear (p — blinkers presumably first time here) is worth noting as a potential sharpener, and while her instinct is to race held-up, the redistribution dynamic means she will need luck in running from a compressed midfield group.

runners_data.name: Kaiko
runners_data.note: Adrian Wintle's 3yo is the most striking profile, dropping from 8f to 5½f having run on firm ground before (a sim-going win reference) and recording a fifth over 8f last time; the trip shortening dramatically could see her race more freely and take up a position further forward than any rival is willing to match, which makes her positionally interesting in this pace-less contest.

races.paceDynamic: With no confirmed front-runner in the field, this 5½f Bath sprint is set to begin cautiously before exploding into a sprint finish from the halfway point. Every runner in the field carries a hold-up profile, meaning no horse is likely to willingly dictate from the front — the early furlongs will be tactical and potentially muddling, with horses jostling for position rather than blazing clear. Kaiko, making the step down from 8f, is the most interesting pace wildcard and could find herself further forward than usual if rivals are reluctant to lead. The race shape strongly favours any runner with the tactical versatility to travel comfortably in a slowly-run bunch and produce a sharp late turn of foot — a closer with a strong finishing kick has the clearest theoretical edge, though with so many hold-up types compressed into midfield, the finish may be chaotic. Several runners including It's A Mugs Game, Elmfield, Honky Tonk Girl, and Nzuri are genuine hold-up horses redistributed into midfield positions on the map because the field holds more off-the-pace types than the race shape can naturally accommodate at the rear — of those, Kodicall and Kaiko are best placed to actually secure their preferred positions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Muddling Pace Bunched Sprint
scenarios.trigger: If no runner commits to the lead early and the field crawls through the first 3f before a frantic scramble home
scenarios.body: The absence of a pace-setter means the field drifts through the early stages at a crawl, compressing into a tight bunch before a frantic dash up the straight; horses with the sharpest acceleration from a compact group will dominate

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Kaiko Sneaks Front
scenarios.trigger: If Kaiko, dropping markedly in trip from 8f, bowls along in front unchallenged and controls a modest tempo
scenarios.body: Stepping down from 8f, Kaiko could stride into an uncontested lead in a field with no natural front-runner and dictate a steadily-run race that rewards stamina and positional awareness; the firm Bath ground suits this shape and a modest gallop could allow the leader to steal an unassailable advantage

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just strong enough to string the field out and hold-up horses get a clean run through to produce their best late effort
scenarios.body: Should any runner push the pace sufficiently to create a true test, the genuine hold-up horses Kodicall and It's A Mugs Game have profiles that could benefit from a straight and clean run at the leaders; however, with multiple horses redistributed out of their natural hold-up slot, getting a clear passage in a bunched finish is far from guaranteed

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Blanket Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the muddling pace creates interference and multiple runners are hampered or switch late, scrambling the result
scenarios.body: A field of six hold-up horses with no dedicated pace-setter is a recipe for crowding and late-race traffic, and in a scenario where the straight becomes congested Honky Tonk Girl or Nzuri could benefit from a gap appearing at the critical moment

watchPoints.text: Watch for Kaiko drifting to the front unchallenged in the early stages — if she gets a cheap lead in this pace-less field, she may be very difficult to peg back on firm Bath ground.

With four runners redistributed from their natural hold-up positions into midfield, the straight could become severely congested — any horse drawn widest and able to find a clear lane will have a significant advantage.
It's A Mugs Game returns after 331 days off; if signs of rustiness appear early, Callum Hutchinson may struggle to manage the hold-up plan effectively in a race that could suddenly quicken sharply.
Nzuri's headgear (blinkers, marked 'p') is a notable first-time application — watch whether this sharpens her early pace and changes her position relative to her usual rear-facing role.

The firm Bath going is consistent across all five races on the card; no horse appears to have a meaningful going concern, but monitor any pre-race withdrawal or market drift that might signal undisclosed ground worries.

races.name: Thank You To Great Western Air Ambulance Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Connie's Rose
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Grace Harris with William Carson aboard; 15 days since last run, wearing a hood and tongue-tie, and her two most recent similar-going runs produced a second — she leads here by default and her firm-ground record is acceptable, but OR 65 at the top of the weights is the key constraint on whether she holds on.
runners_data.comment: Connie's Rose arrives in good nick just 15 days after her last outing, and a second three starts back underlines her consistency at this level; winless in her last six, she'll need to convert, but our rating of 69 marks her as the one to beat here.

runners_data.name: Beerwah
runners_data.note: Won twice over 5f on good ground and returns 11 days after last start for John & Sean Quinn; wears a blinker and will push forward prominently from the gate — in this race shape she is the natural beneficiary if Connie's Rose tires, but her most recent Bath run (8th) is a mild flag.
runners_data.comment: Beerwah landed a win two starts back and has previous experience over today's trip, returning fit on just 11 days' rest; the chief concern is that eighth last time out suggests he can blow hot and cold.

runners_data.name: Nordic Glory
runners_data.note: Michael Attwater's seven-year-old has one firm-ground win from 15 similar-going runs and returns after 39 days off; a genuine hold-up operator ridden by Owen Lewis (5lb claim), he needs the pace to collapse to get involved and the flat, fast Bath 5½f does not naturally play to a late closer.
runners_data.comment: Nordic Glory landed a win three starts back and has experience of today's trip and going, making him a lively threat from stall 1 carrying 125 lb; the concern is that he has been unplaced in his last two outings.

runners_data.name: Candy Warhol
runners_data.note: Scott Dixon's hold-up handicapper has been in reasonable form at similar trips, including a second at Southwell over 6f; Mikkel Mortensen takes the 5lb claim, but with only one firm-ground placing from 15 runs on comparable surfaces, the going edge is modest, and sitting last in a small, controlled-pace field is a hard ask.
runners_data.comment: Candy Warhol has been knocking persistently at the door, finishing second two of his last six starts, and he arrives here race-fit just 10 days on, with experience of today's trip and conditions — the main question is whether he can finally convert that consistency into a win.

runners_data.name: Payforanother Daay
runners_data.note: 56 days off for Simon Hodgson's stable, which has sent out just 2 runners in the last fortnight; a confirmed rear-runner by nature whose position on the pace map is forward of where she will actually race, making her the most difficult to win from in a shape dominated by a comfortable front-runner on fast ground.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked last on our figures, Payforanother Daay is hard to fancy, though he has run over today's distance and going before and returns from a 56-day break potentially freshened up.

races.paceDynamic: Connie's Rose is the lone confirmed front-runner in a five-horse field on a flat Bath 5½f trip in firm conditions, and with Beerwah also prominent-styled, the pair will push forward from the break to establish what should be a clear, uncontested lead for Connie's Rose. Beerwah will press for position immediately behind or alongside, but with no genuine pace duel developing, the tempo is likely to be honest but controlled rather than brutal — exactly the conditions that allow a front-runner to conserve energy through the first two furlongs before quickening. Nordic Glory, Candy Warhol, and Payforanother Daay are all hold-up types tracking from midfield to rear, and on firm ground over this sharp trip they will need either a soft pace collapse or a significant gap in the running to mow down a front-runner who is allowed to roll along uncontested. This race shape strongly favours the front-running/prominent profile: controlled tempo on fast ground over a sprint distance gives the pace-setter every chance to dictate and hold on.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runner Controls Comfortably
scenarios.trigger: If Connie's Rose breaks well and is allowed to dictate a sustainable gallop unchallenged, controlling the race throughout.
scenarios.body: Connie's Rose sets a controlled, measured tempo on fast ground and, untroubled by any rival willing to commit fully to her pace, has the race run to her strengths; Beerwah, the most likely to travel prominently in second, would be the nearest threat if Connie's Rose ties up late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Beerwah tracks Connie's Rose closely and has enough in reserve to collar her inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Beerwah has winning form over 5f on good ground and can sit a length or two off the early pace before producing a finishing effort; if Connie's Rose sets a fraction too brisk a clip in firm conditions, Beerwah's hold on second could convert into a narrow win.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closers Finish Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses significantly in the final furlong, opening a late lane for the trailing trio.
scenarios.body: Nordic Glory's sole firm-ground win gives him a genuine profile claim here, and Candy Warhol has placed twice at the trip and distance combination on similar surfaces; both need either a collapse in pace or a wide, clean passage that rarely materialises in a five-runner sprint on flat ground.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Scrambles Field
scenarios.trigger: If a slow or ragged start resets positions and the race is run in fits and starts rather than fluent front-running rhythm.
scenarios.body: Payforanother Daay, a natural hold-up type shuffled into the midfield map through redistribution and carrying a STYLE_FIT flag, is the least likely to benefit even in this shape as the position shown is not natural; any scrambled finish would most likely hand an unexpected advantage to Beerwah catching a stricken Connie's Rose.

watchPoints.text: Watch Connie's Rose's start — if she breaks cleanly and gets uncontested lead, the race shape is set; a missed break in a five-runner field on firm ground would fundamentally reshape the entire race.

Beerwah's positioning in the first furlong is critical — if she presses Connie's Rose hard early rather than settling in second, a genuine pace duel on firm ground could open the door for the hold-up trio far more than current probabilities suggest.

Nordic Glory's 39-day absence is a layoff flag worth monitoring in-running; if he comes off the bridle sooner than expected tracking from the rear, his chances of reaching the leaders over 5½f evaporate quickly on flat, fast ground.

With only five runners, draw position and early stride pattern will be highly visible from the start — note any horse that is early off the bridle before the two-furlong pole as a sign the pace has been too brisk for the conditions.

Payforanother Daay holds a STYLE_FIT flag and has not raced for 56 days — treat any market move for her with caution, as her redistribution to a midfield map position masks a true rear-of-field running style that is structurally disadvantaged today.

races.name: Great Western Air Ambulance Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Blue Hero
runners_data.note: Proven at 1m and 1m2f on Firm, with a win and placed effort in similar going recently; the 8-year-old's hold-up style is genuinely natural here and Finley Marsh rides a live chance with Adrian Wintle's yard in decent form (2/16 T14).
runners_data.comment: Blue Hero arrives here in fine fettle, just 16 days after a winning effort, and backed that up with a runner-up finish last time out; he has experience of today's trip and going, and from stall 2 off 138 lb, he looks the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Racing Demon
runners_data.note: No wins or places from two runs on Firm (0W0P sim-going) is a significant negative flag; William Carver takes over for Ed de Giles but the hold-up style and a modest recent form string of 57257 give little encouragement on this surface.
runners_data.comment: Racing Demon shaped well when second three starts back, and his experience over today's trip and going, combined with a fitness-friendly 17-day break, makes him a genuine threat from stall 4 — though he remains winless in recent starts and will need to find more late on.

runners_data.name: Offiah's Boy
runners_data.note: Strong recent firm-ground figures (1W1P from 3 runs) are the headline, though his true style is hold-up and he is placed in midfield here only because there are more rear-runners than the map can accommodate — treat his map position with caution.
runners_data.comment: Offiah's Boy has run over today's trip and going, arrives here fresh on a 16-day break, and our rating edges him ahead of his official mark — the concern is that he's been winless in his last five starts, with finishes no better than fifth.

runners_data.name: Hammal
runners_data.note: The ⚠ fades-in-finish flag combined with just one placed effort from seven starts on similar going (0W0P) paints a bleak picture; headgear noted and Callum Hutchinson picks up the ride, but the style mismatch and stamina concerns on firm ground are real discount factors.
runners_data.comment: Hammal has run over today's trip and going before and, sixth on his latest start, bounces back with fitness on his side at just 17 days since his last run — yet winless in his last six starts remains the nagging concern.

runners_data.name: All About George
runners_data.note: Josephine Gordon partners this four-year-old just seven days after his last run, which merits monitoring for freshness; hold-up in style but placed into midfield due to field congestion, and his record of three consecutive Good-ground runs without a win suggests he is yet to find his best surface.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked fifth of six on our figures, All About George faces a stiff task here; he has run over today's trip and returns quickly on seven days' rest, but a tumbling recent profile of 4th, 5th, and 7th makes him hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Miss Colette
runners_data.note: The standout unknown quantity — 338 days off the track for Sir Mark Prescott, who habitually prepares horses patiently for a target, and arriving at a new trip (1m2f) on Firm ground with a yard in strong recent form (7/20 T14); natural hold-up type whose map position reflects genuine style rather than redistribution, making her form string of 7379 on different surfaces hard to read here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and off the track for 338 days, Miss Colette faces a stiff task on these figures, though a third three starts back offers slim encouragement and the trainer is in sharp form at 41% over the past fortnight.

races.paceDynamic: With no confirmed front-runner in this six-runner field on firm ground at Bath over 1m2f, the race is likely to begin at a measured tempo before developing into a sprint finish from the home turn. Every runner in the field carries a hold-up profile, meaning none is likely to take up a genuine pace-forcing role — the field will drift along in a tight bunch, with modest fractions until the pace quickens late. Blue Hero and Racing Demon are the two most credible hold-up performers whose records at least show placed efforts in similar conditions, while Offiah's Boy, Hammal, All About George and Miss Colette are all genuine hold-up types redistributed across the map because too many horses share the same natural position to represent at the rear. The race shape strongly favours the horse who can deliver the sharpest finishing kick from a close-up position in the bunched sprint, making the winner most likely a tactically adaptable runner who stays concentrated through a slow-run race rather than a pure closer needing a strong gallop to make ground.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Bunched Sprint, Best Kick Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the field drifts at a steady pace and the race becomes a dash from two furlongs out with all runners in close proximity.
scenarios.body: With no pace-maker, the entire field will arrive together rounding the final bend and the outcome hinges purely on which horse delivers the sharpest acceleration on firm turf; Blue Hero's two recent wins at 8f on Firm at this trip range give him a meaningful edge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Slow Burn, Late Surge Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is genuinely tardy early and only a powerful late run from off the pace proves rewarding.
scenarios.body: A very slow pace paradoxically suits the horse with the best cruising speed who can switch off and then quicken — Miss Colette, freshened by 338 days off and trained by Sir Mark Prescott, arrives with unknown reserves that could suit this scenario.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Lone Raider Steals Uncontested
scenarios.trigger: If one runner elects to stride forward and set a moderate solo lead, finding no resistance from this otherwise passive group.
scenarios.body: With every rival reluctant to lead, a horse willing to role-reverse and dictate from the front at a controlled tempo on firm ground could find a gap in opposition before rivals realise the race is developing; Offiah's Boy or Hammal drifting to the front through default rather than intention is the trigger.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Firm Ground Attrition Breaks Field
scenarios.trigger: If the firm conditions prove more taxing than expected and the race develops a stronger gallop that exposes stamina weaknesses.
scenarios.body: Racing Demon's sole placed effort on firm came over shorter, while Hammal's repeated fading patterns and poor firm-going record (1/7 sim-going, 0W0P) suggest attrition could eliminate several; a horse with genuine stamina reserves at 1m2f firm would benefit.

watchPoints.text: Blue Hero's two recent Firm-ground wins at comparable distances make him the most course-condition-relevant runner — watch for Finley Marsh to settle him quietly before delivering his challenge from off the pace in the final two furlongs.

Miss Colette's 338-day absence is the single biggest unknown — Sir Mark Prescott's operation routinely has horses fit first time up, but watch the paddock for any signs of a dry coat or unsettled behaviour on the firm ground before drawing conclusions.
Hammal's repeated pattern of fading in the finish could be amplified on firm turf over 1m2f — if the pace quickens early, watch for him to drop away two furlongs out rather than sustain his effort.

With every runner a natural hold-up type, watch the first two furlongs carefully — if no horse moves forward voluntarily, the entire field may crawl and compress, turning this into a five-furlong sprint in disguise from the home bend.

All About George runs just seven days after his last outing — watch whether Josephine Gordon positions him more prominently than his profile suggests, given the absence of any genuine pace to track in this field.
